notes.problem: Seven visual_family labels and six picture payloads promise real variety, but every scene currently repeats the same four depth planes, binder position/scale, pointing engineer position/pose, and almost every truck placement. Each scene names only one camera move and repeats identical visual_events. The bespoke mechanism can supply genuine divergence, but the board still encodes a repeated tableau rather than the promised macro, cab, map and human inspection compositions.
notes.fix: Before animatic, make s2 a true binder-dominant macro, s3 a wide two-leaf assembly, s4 an oblique cab-dominant view, s5 a Texas-dominant view and s7 a hand/page-dominant human action. Keep the binder as continuity but vary its framing. Replace duplicated event descriptions and bind event item_ids to the actual changing objects; document the composed secondary camera move where used.

notes.problem: Sentence-to-pixel must_show and change bindings name only safety-case, omitting evidence-join for claims/evidence assembly, truck for the cab transfer and freight traversal, and engineer for inspection. This permits the declared proof to pass while the literal mechanism is missing or tiny.
notes.fix: Bind s3 to evidence-join plus safety-case, s4 to truck plus safety-case, s6 to truck plus the route-label object, and s7 to engineer plus safety-case. In the animatic those objects must dominate the corresponding payoff rather than sit behind the binder.

notes.problem: The narration establishes Texas as a planned initial market, but inspectionMap carries county Dallas and the animation description moves a planned truck toward mapped territory. A Dallas pin or directional route would make a more specific launch claim than the sentence.
notes.fix: Show the whole Texas outline as an inset of the June filing with PLANNED remaining visible. Do not render a Dallas launch pin or route unless the validated claim separately supports that location.

notes.problem: An autonomousRig with mode existing placed immediately after a launch-market map can read silently as an existing driverless Dallas-to-Houston route. The correcting status lives only on a long binder label, so an unreadable label would invert the point.
notes.fix: Make EXISTING FREIGHT and DRIVERLESS LAUNCH STILL PLANNED separately prominent during the actual crossing. Keep the pending launch object visibly detached from the existing route. If source validation confirms an onboard safety driver, show that evidence-specific distinction; otherwise do not invent one.

notes.problem: The close says year-end is the target, but no board item or must_show supplies year-end. Its binder props repeat WORK REMAINS and the opening state, so mute viewers learn neither the target nor the next step.
notes.fix: Put YEAR-END TARGET on the amber bookmark and retain VERIFICATION + VALIDATION PENDING on the last exposed leaf, with both supplied by board props and named in proof. Then fold the paper road into the case around the pending leaf. This preserves the button while answering what happens next.

strongest_frame: s4. The readiness percentage visibly detaching from the windshield and attaching to the evidence binder makes the central metric distinction physical. Preserve this transfer as one continuous motion and never render a percentage as trip-safety odds.
weakest_frame: s8. As written it repeats the opening binder and WORK REMAINS while leaving the narrated year-end target invisible. The bookmark can make the close earn its time.
review_scope: Board only. No rendered-frame, audio or source-validation claims. The described bespoke episode implementation was considered as intended execution, not as verified footage.
